# Paper statement inventory · `reg:inventory:overview`

**Setup (Scope)** · `setup:inventory:scope` The inventory contains 1645 statement rows and 2801 constant entries. The paper release is network-v0.29.1. The inventory covers explicit labels and labels generated by structure and frontier environments at this release; the two censuses are separate. Each refresh re-reads every inventory row against the new release and rewrites current_at to that release; it records the text reflected by the row, not when the row was introduced. The constants field refreshed_at likewise identifies its projection edition. The inventory distinguishes 1608 explicit labels and 37 environment-generated labels; neither census silently substitutes for the other. Implementation kinds and proposed homes are engineering classifications, not claims that code exists or that a paper question is settled. The decomposition is recorded in (`rec:decomposition:decision`). A kind or home of none assigns no new implementation item or no Layer 1 home, respectively; documentation can still have an owner.

**Convention (Label presentation)** · `conv:inventory:labels` Paper labels are exhibited with doubled delimiters because the imported registry format is unavailable under the repository namespace. The citable field preserves eligibility under the adopted kind relation for a project-neutral import format; it does not claim that an import is active. Paper label kinds remain unchanged. Environment text is the inventory's recorded description, while implementation kind describes a proposed code responsibility. Short subdivision rows locate separately labelled cases, conditions and steps; their titles do not replace the normative statement or supply its premises.

| G Frontiers | ``app:frontiers`` | appendix | Inventory open questions affecting comparator claims and specified architectural extensions, each with scope, requirements and stake. One Layer-1 open problem concerns sharp funded-partition guarantees; six entries are architectural extensions, and neither universal splitting invariance nor universal burn monotonicity remains an open assertion. | none | pn-verification | True | network-v0.29.1; explicit |
| G Frontiers | ``def:frontiers:open-problem`` | definition | An open problem must be capable of changing a needed admission, faithfulness or convergence claim or requirement; an already proved bound or a deployment choice with fixed validation is not one merely because it could be sharpened. One Layer-1 open problem concerns sharp funded-partition guarantees, beside six architectural extensions. | none | none | True | network-v0.29.1; explicit |
| G Frontiers | ``rem:frontiers:priority`` | remark | Prioritize sharp funded-partition guarantees for faithfulness, exact conserved evaluation and the boundary mechanism for implementation, with declared work envelopes and certificate/emission monitoring. A tighter certificate requires a specified stronger charter; proved counterexamples and invariants delimit the remaining questions. | policy | pn-host | True | network-v0.29.1; explicit |
| G Frontiers | ``subsec:frontiers:core`` | subsection | Distinguish the remaining funded-partition questions from their evidence and stake in comparator claims. Neither the open status nor its evidence licenses a new rule without stated hypotheses and consequences. | none | none | False | network-v0.29.1; explicit |
| G Frontiers | ``frontier:allocation-split-invariance`` | frontier (core) | General funded-partition invariance is false. Keep sharp advantage bounds, structural invariant partitions and controlled admission/reward comparisons open; pair totals, closed weighted means and equal-rate invariants survive, and concentration can approach a whole hull width. | none | none | False | network-v0.29.1; environment |

| G Frontiers | ``frontier:boundary-mechanism`` | frontier (arch) | Expose accepted-set agreement and duration accountability without inventing decentralized consensus. | policy | pn-host | False | network-v0.29.1; environment |

| G Frontiers | ``frontier:typed-sign-transport`` | frontier (arch) | Keep composing path coherence distinct from locally gated stance. ## Constants · `sec:inventory:constants`

**Observation (Source definitions)** · `obs:inventory:constants` Empty class and citation fields preserve absence in the released collection. The dataset retains source literal strings, expressions, function selectors and display rules in its definition field; a function selector is not an evaluated numeric result or a certificate. It contains 2799 declarations and the separate standing_profile and verification_fixtures records. The verification profile retains the published exact inputs, precision and comparison settings for the released finite witnesses; their scope is the declared fixtures, not a universal performance or economic claim. The latter preserves exact rational strings for hop shape, depth masses, self-retention and certified strength, plus the domain-weight mode, grounding the reference case in ``ver:standing:conserved-equilibrium-enclosure``. The input schema is peer-constants-2; the added profile does not imply that old readers understand its additional member. Generated decimal displays alone supply no numerical proof.

**Model (Reference standing profile)** · `model:inventory:standing-profile` The exact hop shape is 1, 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, the normalized depth masses are 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/8, self-retention is 1, domain weighting is uniform_unit, and certified strength is 1. No intermediate rung grid is inferred from this reference declaration; deployment grids remain separate.

**Open Question (Bridge reaction placement)** · `open:inventory:bridge-reaction-placement` Owner: the deploying operator for the published centralized-phase reaction, and the repository architecture reviewer, the role that reviews scope and crate-responsibility changes for repository acceptance, for resolving the implementation boundary. ``case:transport:bridge-eligibility-cliff`` requires the threshold, share-volatility companion and conditional reference-rule publication; ``rem:bridge:eligibility-cliff-primary`` makes flip frequency a distribution-stability measure. The existing responsibility map gives pn-readouts published standing/title and optional raw views, and pn-host package publication, while placing bridge computation, guild policy and CAN outside the implementation (`conv:design:scope`), (`rec:decomposition:decision`). It does not assign computation of bridge selection and normalized-share history, so neither crate is inferred as owner. Settle the question either through a deployment-owned computation over published epoch certificates, recording its metric and publication contract, or through an accepted scope amendment assigning that computation and contract to a crate; until then these rows retain kind policy and no crate. The publication obligation is required even though adopting its terminal reference rule remains optional.

**Open Question (Deployment terminal evidence placement)** · `open:inventory:deployment-terminal-evidence` Owner: the deploying operator for terminal consumers and their published measurements, and the repository architecture reviewer, the role reviewing scope and crate-responsibility changes, for any implementation assignment. The cadence/maturity, payload/cache and terminal-regression duties of ``cond:deployment:cadence-maturity``, ``cond:deployment:payload-cache-envelope`` and ``cond:deployment:terminal-regression`` include CAN, bridge or application measurements outside (`conv:design:scope`). Existing bites supply canonical epoch certificates, optional raw service and conformance inputs, but do not assign those consumers or cache deployments to a crate. Settle each duty by a deployment-owned measurement contract over published outputs, or by an accepted scope amendment assigning its implementation; these inventory rows assign no new crate or bite. A required deployment comparison is not an implemented Layer-1 feature.
